static_traits.name: Fu Beisha
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; never received psychological counseling or had similar psychological problems before
static_traits.language_features: Negative attitude; able to clearly express own feelings and thoughts; speech rate and logical features not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: I persistently feel not good enough and frustrated about my height, believing I will always be short, which has led to decreased self-esteem and hopelessness. The problem started in adolescence and has intensified recently; once, not being able to reach the cookie jar in the kitchen cabinet triggered these feelings, and I have since avoided height-related situations (e.g. reaching for things up high), ruminating about height and life achievements before sleep, which affects my sleep.
basic_info.core_demands: Realizes height-related thoughts are affecting daily life and self-esteem, hoping to improve this impact through psychological counseling.
growth_experiences: In adolescence I was always shorter than most peers, often teased by others about my height, feeling low self-esteem and hopelessness for a long time; although there are family and friends to confide in, I never talked to them about my height distress, and this forbearance and non-expression gradually solidified into tendencies of negative self-evaluation and social avoidance.

core_beliefs: I will never be good enough
People will not take me seriously

special_situations.event: Not being able to reach the cookie jar in the kitchen cabinet
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot even reach items placed high up, it shows I am very incompetent, and my height will always limit me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding all height-related scenarios, e.g. trying not to reach for items placed high up
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will always be this short; I am helpless

special_situations.event: Every night before sleep, repeatedly thinks about own height and life achievements
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am short, it means my life's achievements will be limited; overall I am just not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continuously ruminating on negative thoughts, trying to solve them through thinking, but actually worsening insomnia and emotions
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My height will always hold me back; I will never get better

special_situations.event: When socializing with peers, worries height will become a problem, relationships become strained as a result
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my height inadequacy is exposed in front of others, I will be looked down upon or laughed at
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding activities with peers, reduced socializing to evade being judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will not take me seriously

special_situations.event: Being late for class due to lack of motivation; academics affected
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot change my height and my performance is not perfect, there is no point in trying
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Procrastinates and arrives late to escape being evaluated or possible failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Anyway I will not do well

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be treated equally and taken seriously, gaining recognition rather than being defined by height
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being laughed at, looked down upon, and rejected because of height; fearing appearing incompetent and like a failure
defense_goal: Through avoidance and distancing, reduces exposure to others' evaluation
Lowers self-expectations to avoid disappointment and shame

object_relations.self_representation: Short, a 'not-good-enough person' who is easily laughed at
object_relations.object_representation: Others are people who are picky, slighting, and mocking of oneself

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to share height distress or express vulnerability with others (including the counselor)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others will consider this problem 'childish/ridiculous', and thus despise or reject oneself
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: With restrained language, responding briefly or avoiding details; in a hesitant tone, lowering emotional intensity, using words like 'nothing' and 'not worth mentioning' to dilute.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When he needs to directly face height-related situations in social settings (such as going out with peers or possibly needing to retrieve objects from high places)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others will belittle or mock oneself; communication will only bring more shame
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Declining or canceling plans on the grounds of worrying what others think; using hypothetical phrasing ('they will definitely laugh at me') to reinforce withdrawal, in a strongly defensive tone.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When facing tasks requiring performance or evaluation (such as attending class on time, finishing homework)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: If I cannot do it perfectly it equals failure, and effort is meaningless
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Postponing or being late on the grounds of 'not feeling well / height causing inconvenience', in a flat but firm tone, emphasizing objective excuses to reduce guilt.

manifestations: Avoiding spending time with peers for fear of being looked down upon because of height; relationship tension and self-isolation
Not yet confiding height distress to family and friends, bearing it alone for a long time
Before sleep, repeatedly thinks about height and life achievements, believing height will always hinder oneself
outcomes: Decreased drive and being late for class

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent Self-denial ('I will never be good enough')
Excessively caring whether others treat me sincerely
Withdrawing in social and classroom settings due to self-reproach

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Having friends and family to talk to yet not expressing distress for a long time, choosing to bear it alone
Turning social energy into self-rumination and insomnia

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Presupposing before socializing that 'others will not take me seriously'
Avoids gatherings or collaboration in advance for fear of being slighted

positive_force: Having artistic talents and a sense of humor
Has potential support resources from family and friends (though not yet shared, support is available)
Willing to seek psychological counseling and try small-step changes
Able to identify and name negative automatic thoughts and cognitive patterns
negative_force: Prominent negative cognitive patterns such as catastrophizing, jumping to conclusions, overgeneralization, and all-or-nothing thinking
Social and situational avoidance, increasing isolation and relationship tension
Ruminating before sleep leading to insomnia, further weakening state and motivation
Lateness and low motivation in academics, causing performance to suffer

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids height-related situations (such as reaching for objects in high places, or scenes in peer activities that might expose a height disadvantage)
antecedent: Needing to reach for items up high
When planning to go out with peers or participate in activities, worries about height being noticed
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing about height and mind-reading inferences (others will look down on / laugh at me), accompanied by shame and hopelessness
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential humiliation and negative evaluation to relieve anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal tension and self-isolation, increasing loneliness and impaired self-esteem

antecedent: Before sleep, thinks about height and life achievements and begins ruminating on negative content
target_behavior.core_reason: Overgeneralization and catastrophic reasoning leading to persistent Self-denial and a sense of meaninglessness
target_behavior.function: Tries to gain a sense of control and resolution through thinking (actually intensifies the emotions)
target_behavior.consequence: Declining sleep quality, low mood, insufficient motivation and being late the next day

target_behavior.behavior: Being late for class and insufficient academic motivation
antecedent: Thinking about height and fear of judgment before class
Getting up in the morning to face study tasks
target_behavior.core_reason: Black-and-white thinking and hopelessness (if not perfect then it equals failure)
target_behavior.function: Avoiding situations of being evaluated and possible failure to reduce immediate anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Academic performance impaired, negative self-evaluation further reinforced
